polls.description: Major shifts in OpenAI's business relationships including the end of Microsoft exclusivity and new partnerships signal a transformation in AI industry alliances.
polls.question: Is OpenAI's break from Microsoft exclusivity good or bad for innovation?

cluster_stories.title: Elon Musk takes the stand in high-profile trial against OpenAI
cluster_stories.summary: Elon Musk officially began his testimony in the trial he has brought against OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and company president Greg Brockman. The three were on the initial founding team of OpenAI, with Musk investing up to $38 million early on before the co-founders' relationship soured over disagreements over company structure and mission, including whether […]
cluster_stories.headline: ELON TAKES THE STAND... OpenAI Trial Begins

cluster_stories.title: The next phase of the Microsoft OpenAI partnership
cluster_stories.summary: OpenAI and Microsoft announce an amended agreement that simplifies the partnership, adds long-term clarity, and supports continued AI innovation at scale.
cluster_stories.headline: OPENAI-MICROSOFT PARTNERSHIP ENTERS NEW PHASE... MAJOR SHIFT

cluster_stories.title: Microsoft to end exclusive license for OpenAI's technology
cluster_stories.summary: Microsoft's exclusive hold on OpenAI's artificial intelligence models is over. This change allows OpenAI to offer its technology to competitors like Amazon and Google. Microsoft will still be OpenAI's main cloud partner and has licensing rights until 2032. This development impacts the ongoing artificial intelligence race.
cluster_stories.headline: Microsoft Loses EXCLUSIVE License to OpenAI Technology

cluster_stories.title: OpenAI’s Altman ‘stole a charity’, Musk claims as trial begins
cluster_stories.summary: Opening arguments kick off legal battle over whether the $850bn start-up sold out its non-profit mission
cluster_stories.headline: MUSK CLAIMS Altman 'Stole a Charity'... Trial Begins

cluster_stories.title: Google expands Pentagon’s access to its AI after Anthropic’s refusal
cluster_stories.summary: After Anthropic refused to allow the DoD to use its AI for domestic mass surveillance and autonomous weapons, Google has signed a new contract with the department.
cluster_stories.headline: GOOGLE EXPANDS PENTAGON AI ACCESS AFTER ANTHROPIC REFUSAL

cluster_stories.title: Amazon Inks Deal with OpenAI, Plans New AWS Applications
cluster_stories.summary: Amazon Web Services announced a partnership with OpenAI a day after that company ended its exclusivity deal with Microsoft. Amazon also plans to sell AI-powered productivity software for the office. AWS CEO Matt Garman speaks with Bloomberg Tech’s Ed Ludlow. (Source: Bloomberg)
cluster_stories.headline: AMAZON PARTNERS WITH OPENAI After Microsoft Deal Ends

cluster_stories.title: Google and Pentagon reportedly agree on deal for ‘any lawful’ use of AI
cluster_stories.summary: Google has signed a classified deal that allows the US Department of Defense to use its AI models for "any lawful government purpose," The Information reports. The agreement was reported less than a day after Google employees demanded CEO Sundar Pichai block the Pentagon from using its AI amid concerns that it would be used […]
cluster_stories.headline: GOOGLE SIGNS SECRET PENTAGON AI DEAL... 'ANY LAWFUL PURPOSE'

cluster_stories.title: Amazon Launches AI Productivity Software for Office Workers
cluster_stories.summary: Amazon.com Inc.’s cloud unit, best known for providing technology infrastructure to corporations, is looking to sell AI-powered productivity software for the office.
cluster_stories.headline: AMAZON LAUNCHES AI Office Software... Takes on Microsoft

cluster_stories.title: OpenAI breaks free of Microsoft's cloud
cluster_stories.summary: Article URL: https://www.axios.com/2026/04/28/openai-microsoft-cloud-amazon Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=47935716 Points: 2 # Comments: 1
cluster_stories.headline: OPENAI BREAKS FREE FROM MICROSOFT CLOUD

cluster_stories.title: Google signs classified AI deal with Pentagon: Report
cluster_stories.summary: Google has joined other tech firms in a deal with the US Department of Defense. The agreement allows the Pentagon to use Google's AI for lawful government purposes. This includes sensitive work like mission planning and weapons targeting. The Pentagon is signing deals worth up to $200 million with major AI labs. Google's agreement includes adjustments to AI safety settings.
cluster_stories.headline: GOOGLE SIGNS CLASSIFIED AI DEAL WITH PENTAGON

polls.description: Breaking partnerships and new alliances reshape the AI landscape as Microsoft loses OpenAI exclusivity while Google secures Pentagon contracts.
